chunks: In his bequest to al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Seek assistance with some of this [world] for this [hereafter], and do not become a burden upon the people.

key_terms.كُلُولًا: Plural of 'kall', meaning one who is a burden, dependent, or lacking in self-sufficiency; a person who relies on others for basic needs
key_terms.هَذِهِ عَلَى هَذِهِ: A rhetorical ellipsis meaning 'this world for this hereafter'; both demonstrative pronouns are feminine, referring to dunya (this world) and akhira (the hereafter)
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٌ: A bequest or written testament; here, al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi' recorded the Imam's words in a formal bequest to al-Mufaddal

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about using worldly resources for the hereafter and not being a burden on others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs that one should use worldly means and resources to secure provisions for the hereafter, while simultaneously being self-sufficient and not relying on others for one's daily needs. This teaching was transmitted through al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi' in his written bequest to al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, a trusted companion of the Imam. The phrase 'this upon this' is a rhetorically concise reference — the first 'this' refers to the dunya (worldly life and its resources), while the second 'this' refers to the akhira (the hereafter), urging believers to balance material engagement with spiritual goals.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Al Rabi’e in his bequest to Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘Seek assistance with some of this upon this, and do not become a burden upon the people’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi‘ in his (Imam’s) advice to al- Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
You should use certain items of these resources to overcome other tasks and do not become a burden on people.’”
